title: decisions query side (active, search, archive, tag) — renderer split out to rpl-10
action:
Port the decisions QUERY verbs only: active, search, archive, tag (lib at packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:739 archiveDecisions, :810 the active projection; handlers in packages/bee/bee.mjs:1924-2229). The index renderer and its --check drift verdict were SPLIT OUT into rpl-10 on review (this cell was over the plan's own reference size). archive and tag are read-modify-write and take the same D9 lock as the write path — consume crates/bee-core/src/lock.rs, never reimplement. search supports --tag / --scope / OR-ranked multi-term --text / --all over the archive; reproduce each ranking comparator at its own call site rather than unifying them. REVIEW-FOUND FIXTURE GAP: `queen-bench --generate` produces monotone filler — every decisions row is type `decide` with an identical date, no tags, and there are no supersede or redact rows (crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs:287), and no .bee/decisions-archive.jsonl at all. Every scenario below is therefore non-discriminating unless it SEEDS what it asserts, using the per-scenario seeding rpl-1 provides on top of the baseline store. Register --cmd-check scenarios: search across every filter incl. a multi-term text query whose ranking separates candidates; search --tag over seeded tags; archive with the store at and past its threshold, with a seeded archive sidecar; tag on a missing id; active with seeded superseded AND redacted entries present; and this group's unknown-verb usage fallback line (packages/bee/bee.mjs:6586-6609). TWO ITEMS CARRIED FROM THE rpl-4 GOAL-CHECK, both in this group and both owed here. (1) COMPOSED-HANDLER GAP. rpl-4's sweep-with-hits path had its two COMPONENTS oracle-compared, but the composed handler was not: crates/queen-bee/src/ledger/decisions.rs:272-293 (the per-hit capture-stub loop) and :295-313 (the `Propagation sweep: N citation(s)` header plus the two-space-indented `{file}:{line}  {excerpt}` hit lines) have no oracle test and no --cmd-check scenario. A reviewer read them against packages/bee/bee.mjs:1975-1992 and they matched textually, but a read is not an executed assertion. Close it here: the sweep-with-hits output cannot go through --cmd-check (the fresh event uuid sits as an ARRAY ELEMENT under dids and inside outcome prose, which normalize.rs's key-gated deny-by-default masking cannot reach, and widening it to pattern masking would blind rpl-3's capture surface), so add an ORACLE test that drives the composed handler on both runtimes over a docs tree with real citation hits and compares stdout plus the resulting capture-queue rows against the frozen mjs. (2) UTF-16 INCONSISTENCY. crates/bee-core/src/decisions.rs:869 computes short8 as target_id.chars().take(8) — SCALAR VALUES — while packages/bee/lib/decisions.mjs:465 uses targetId.slice(0, 8) — UTF-16 CODE UNITS. Unreachable for uuids but reachable in principle, since supersede accepts an arbitrary id (the conformance suite itself uses a non-uuid). The same file already handles this correctly in js_excerpt, so it is an inconsistency, not an unknown: make short8 use the same code-unit helper and pin it with an astral-character case. 

REWORK ROUND 2 — the goal-check returned NEEDS_REVISION on this cell. THE BUG, measured by the judge on identical store clones with host TZ=Asia/Bangkok and identical argv `decisions archive --before 2026-07-26T00:00:00 --json`: mjs archived [..001] and kept 2; queen-bee archived [..001, ..003] and kept 1. BOTH exited 0 with no warning. queen-bee pruned an extra row from .bee/decisions.jsonl because it read the offset-less cutoff as ...T00:00:00Z while V8 read it as +07:00, i.e. 17:00Z the previous day. The read side diverges the same way: `search --since 2026-07-26T00:00:00` gives mjs [bbbb, cccc] versus queen-bee [bbbb]. Root cause: crates/bee-core/src/jsdate.rs:224, where the None-or-empty designator arm silently means UTC; consumed at crates/bee-core/src/decisions.rs:1073 (the archive cutoff) and crates/queen-bee/src/ledger/decisions.rs:560,613. On a negative-offset host the error inverts into UNDER-archiving. This matters because `archive` DELETES rows from the active store, has no inverse verb, and the pruned store is what `decisions active` and rpl-8's feedback aggregator read. THE FIX, and it is deliberately the small fail-closed one: make the None offset arm return None so an offset-less date-time becomes the same LOUD REFUSAL the V8 legacy-fallback forms already produce, rather than a silent wrong cut. Do NOT try to reproduce ECMA-262 local time — that needs a local-offset source std does not have, and guessing it would trade a detectable divergence for an undetectable one. The documented surface is unaffected: date-only forms ARE UTC in ECMA-262 and the judge's 77-candidate fuzz through the real binaries found zero divergence there, so `--before 2099-01-01` keeps working. THEN close the coverage gap that let this through: every --since/--before in the harness today is either a full toISOString() value or an obviously-invalid string, so the registry's own documented `--before 2099-01-01` — the exact call that motivated writing date_parse_ms — has NO --cmd-check scenario. Add one. ALSO widen the declared non-reproduction list in jsdate.rs, which the judge found INCOMPLETE: lowercase `z`, a space separator instead of `T`, `+HHmm` without a colon, and expanded-year `+00YYYY` forms are all the same fail-closed class and are currently undeclared. FINALLY, record but do not necessarily fix: for `2026/01/01`-shaped input both runtimes exit 1 with DIFFERENT error text, a stderr divergence no scenario covers — either pin it as a declared artifact the way rpl-11 did for the readJson warning, or state in the worker block why it is acceptable to leave unpinned.

trace.outcome: Round 2: closed the goal-check's NEEDS_REVISION. An offset-less date-time (2026-07-26T00:00:00) now FAILS CLOSED in bee_core::jsdate instead of being silently read as UTC — the judge's own reproduction (mjs archived 1 keeping 2, the port archived 2 keeping 1, both exit 0, on a +07:00 host) is now an executed test that fails against the pre-fix code. Fail-closed by choice, not limitation: emulating ECMA-262 local time needs an offset source std lacks, and guessing one trades a visible divergence for an invisible one. Closed the coverage hole that let it through — the documented date-only --before form now has two cross-runtime scenarios, one of which resolves the cutoff instant to the millisecond. Widened the declared non-reproduction list with the four measured same-class forms the judge found undeclared, and pinned the 2026/01/01 stderr wording divergence as a declared artifact. decisions group 36 -> 38 scenarios, all zero-diff with all controls firing.
